key_insight: A drilled-to-bossed joint geometry combined with tuned DDFW parameters substantially improves AA2024-T351 weld strength, while deep learning can predict tensile performance with moderate accuracy.
engineering_relevance: The study offers a practical route to stronger lightweight aluminum joints for aerospace and automotive applications by linking joint design, process optimization, and data-driven prediction.
method: L18 orthogonal array experiments on AA2024-T351 in direct drive friction welding
Compared friction pressure, forging pressure, spindle speed, faying-surface geometry, and friction time
Trained deep learning models (ensemble residual, compact attention, adaptive multiscale) to predict ultimate tensile strength
evidence_signal: The best parameter set (30 MPa friction pressure, 70 MPa forging pressure, 2200 rpm, drilled-to-bossed geometry, 4 min) achieved 538 MPa tensile strength and 325 MPa torsional strength, and the best model reached R² ≈ 0.81.
watch_item: The predictive model accuracy is still limited enough that broader validation on independent weld datasets and operating conditions would be needed before deployment.
paper_title: Enhancing weld performance of AA2024-T351 using drilled-to-bossed geometry and deep learning prediction in direct drive friction welding
